cells.tense: The light is lit right now, and it is spent toward other people.
cells.act: stand in the gap it leaves without rebuilding yet
cells.ask: There is something you hold up for someone else without being asked. Set it down this week and leave the gap where it was — no repair, no quiet substitution. Watch what the week does without your hands in it.
cells.core: Nothing here pulls you away from people. You do the work, and what comes out of it meets someone where they are — the skill lives in the contact, not only in the quiet room. That is the test of whether the practice is yours, and it is passing. Solitude is not a wall in this; something in it feeds what arrives when you are with someone. When you are mid-refine and a person speaks, you can tell whether the refining is in service or in hiding, and the body registers it before words arrive. There is a rule you keep in the practice because dropping it would feel disloyal. That rule is the next thing meant to come down, and it comes down when you stop propping it. The light is already doing its work through your hands and out into the room.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is not a cell. It opens toward people, and that is the test.
cells.verb: keeping a small steady light lit by attention rather than flash
cells.place: where what someone else feels lands in your own body and asks to be answered

cells.tense: You are bracing against the end of a session that has not started yet.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Stop one session early, mid-rep, on purpose, and set the work aside. Then leave the space that opens unfilled. No substitute task, no making up the minutes later.
cells.core: The refining has outrun the doing. You know the version of yourself who has this skill, and the current one keeps losing to that version, so sessions get watched instead of entered, and stopping reads as falling behind rather than as a breach of what you actually care about. People feel this even when you say nothing. They come close and meet the one holding everything up rather than the one doing the work. The grip isn't really about them; it is about what would happen in the hours left open. But setting the work down is not a lost thread. It is how the thread gets to be yours instead of the hand's. A session ended early on purpose teaches more than another hour of holding on.
cells.sheetLine: The grip has become the practice. Set it down anyway.

cells.tense: The light went out some time back, and you have stood at that door since.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: When someone reaches toward you with an hour, a turn, a small help — take it and keep it. Let it come your way once without sending it back.
cells.core: The body stays careful around practice, and careful is how it has stayed. You may not put it that way. What shows is that repetition carries nothing now: you pick things up, the picking-up runs dry before it becomes a habit, and you cannot tell whether the work is missing or you are. Something underneath has not been getting anything back. You have been putting into the practice and into the people around it, and taking neither credit nor return. The repair is not more effort in the practice itself. Exchange has to run two directions before the light can find you again, and it can start as small as letting an hour arrive and stay.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange has been running one way. That is what went out.

cells.tense: You are practising in this very moment, and the account you give leaves practice out.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Before you begin the next thing you are already good at, look only as far as that one step. Take it without a plan for the one after. Let the rest stay dark a while.
cells.core: The refinements arrive in your life as though they came free. You can read a room in a way you could not before, people point it out, and your answer is that it just happens. It does not just happen. A rhythm sits underneath your days, built by attention, and your account of yourself skips the building. There may even be a story that you are not someone who practises — after what it once cost, the story makes sense. But the story and the rhythm are different things. You don't have to take the story apart. You only have to know the step you take next is one you are choosing, even quietly, with no map past it. Enough light for that step is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You are practising right now. The account you give omits it.

attempts.check: The claim about the Too Little cell — that practice has come to feel dangerous because of past experience — is an inference from the status, not from anything the person has said; they could answer that they simply stopped and nothing dramatic happened. The Too Much cell says the person fears what happens if they stop, which is a motive the record can't confirm; if that reads wrong, the ask still gives them an actual hour back whether or not the fear is real. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'The solitude is your own construction' — it sounds like insight but the record only says isolation feels necessary, not that the person built it. I've pulled these back to what the record supports: what the capacity is doing, not why.
